summary: Forest Service lookout in Jackson County, KY; about 80 ft per 1936 item; Register says circa 1937 build and mid-1970s demolition; S-Tree Campground now nearby.

facts.design: Tower about 80 ft tall per a 1936 newspaper item; type not given
facts.status_note: Demolished in the mid-1970s per the Register; a Forest Service campground named S-Tree is in the area, and a campground guide places the tower near its entrance

access.note: S-Tree Campground is open and first-come, first-served; no source says whether the tower spot itself is open to visitors

events.note: An April 30, 1936 newspaper item already mentions the S-tree tower, about 80 feet tall; this predates the Register's circa 1937 build date
Register gives a build date of circa 1937 by the Forest Service
Register says demolished in the mid-1970s; 1975 is an approximation, no exact year given
Registered December 31, 2023 as US 2100, KY 6; nominated by Linda and Robert Wittenback

evidence.supports: built by the Forest Service around 1937
evidence.quote: S-Tree Lookout was built by the U.S. Forest Service around 1937.
The tower was demolished in the mid-1970s.

evidence.supports: Forest Service maintains a campground in the area
evidence.quote: The Forest Service maintains a campground in the area.

evidence.supports: the S-tree tower already existed by 1936, at Sand Gap
evidence.quote: There is such a project on turning off to the right at Sand Gap, at the S-tree tower.

evidence.supports: tower some 80 feet; view twelve miles around on clear days
evidence.quote: People can mount the tower, some 80 feet, and on clear days can have a view twelve miles around.

evidence.supports: planned picnic tables and places for a fire
evidence.quote: Picnic tables are to be provided and places for having a fire.

evidence.supports: campground on a ridge above Horse Lick Creek near McKee, Jackson County
evidence.quote: S-Tree Campground sits on a ridge above Horse Lick Creek near McKee in Jackson County, KY.
Each of the 20 first-come, first-served campsites has a picnic table, tent pad, fire ring and lantern pole.

evidence.supports: S-Tree fire tower once stood near the campground entrance
evidence.quote: S-Tree Fire Tower once stood near the entrance to the campground.
Road access is worth planning around.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives circa 1937; a 1936 newspaper item already describes the S-tree tower. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Height comes only from the 1936 item (some 80 feet), so it is an approximate figure. The campground sources are current; they do not say whether the tower spot is on campground ground. The Dyrt is a commercial campground guide, used only for the tower's location near the entrance. The Register's December 2023 photo credit (Linda and Robert Wittenback) has no image URL in the fetched text; no photo added.
